chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Shah narrated to us, saying: Abu Hamid Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hussein narrated to us, saying: Abu Yazid Ahmad ibn Khalid al-Khalidy narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Salih al-Tamimi narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: Anas ibn Muhammad (Abu Malik) narrated to me, from his father, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them), from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) that he said in his will to him:
O Ali! Hasten to utilize four [things] before four [events]: utilize your youth before your old age, your health before your illness, your wealth before your poverty, and your life before your death.
ai.seo_question: What are the four things one should utilize before they are lost according to the Prophet's will to Ali?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Khisal* via the pristine chain of the Ahl al-Bayt, this hadith emphasizes the urgency of utilizing life's transient blessings for spiritual preparation. It serves as a cornerstone of Shia ethical instruction, urging believers to convert periods of youth, health, wealth, and life into enduring merit before their inevitable transition to old age, sickness, poverty, and death.
